youtube.title: JAN RIVERS
youtube.summary: Jan Rivers, spokeswoman for Genspect New Zealand and Public Good, discusses the High Court’s ruling on the government’s puberty blocker restrictions. She argues that the case focused on consultation and legal process rather than a full assessment of the medical evidence and says opposing perspectives were given insufficient weight. With prescriptions continuing and an appeal being sought, Jan says that the debate over children’s welfare and future policy is far from over. For more from Jan visit Public Good & Genspect or find Jan on X and Substack

youtube.title: MEDIA MATTERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Marty Gibson examine the Chris Luxon–Chris Hipkins debate, arguing that the major parties are increasingly alike and questioning media criticism of MMP’s overhang strategy. They discuss New Zealand’s rising government debt, proposed social media controls and Green and Te Pāti Māori MPs’ engagement with gangs, debating how to address gang crime without romanticising it or ignoring its victims. For further information: Stuff | Inside The Green & Te Pāti Māori catch up with the Mongrel Mob NZ Government Debt Clock For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart

youtube.title: MICHAEL LAWS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan chats with Michael Laws, Otago Regional Councillor and New Zealand First candidate for Waitaki, about the erosion of public trust, which he traces to Rogernomics and the rise of economic liberalism. Michael argues that powerful elites and cartels disadvantage ordinary New Zealanders, calls for university reform, discusses the Treaty of Waitangi and social division and warns that National’s two-tick strategy could hand the election to the centre-left. For more on Michael Laws or find him on Facebook For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday and find out everything about the overhang, wasted vote and tactical voting at Vote Smart

youtube.title: MARK KAPLAN
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan interviews Health Truth founder Mark Kaplan, whose heart attack at 52 prompted him to question conventional approaches to chronic disease. Mark explains his vision for Neo, an AI-powered health platform designed to analyse personal health data, connect users with doctors and challenge pharmaceutical influence. They discuss root-cause health, nutrition, metabolic disease and the goal of extending healthspan rather than simply lifespan. For more information: Visit the HealthTruth website or check out Neo Root or Neo and the Unplugged Movement Find Mark on X
